prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics: algebra, trigonometry, vector calculus

learning_outcomes.text: Students know and can describe the importance of statics within engineering.
They can name and explain the axioms of statics of rigid bodies.
They know the different types of loads on technical constructions and can name and classify them.
They know the difference between internal and external stresses and can explain them.
They can name the acting quantities (force, moment) and mechanical engineering components of a complete system (pendulum support, disc, beam) and explain their properties.
Identify and classify bearings and connections of mechanical systems.
Break down larger systems into subsystems.
Create free-body diagrams of complete and partial systems.
Distinguish between pointwise and distributed forces and take them into account accordingly.
Based on the free-body diagrams, set up and solve the equilibrium conditions for two-dimensional and simple three-dimensional systems.
Calculate loads on bearings and connections.
Calculate and graphically represent internal forces in beams.
Calculate linear and area centroids of planar bodies.
Identify friction points in mechanical systems, distinguish between static and kinetic friction, and calculate the acting friction forces.
Prepare and document problems, solutions, and solution paths in an engineering-appropriate manner.
Students are able to abstract a mechanical engineering construction to such an extent that it can be calculated for a mechanical design using the learned methods.
Students can carry out the first steps and calculations necessary for the strength-based design of a mechanical construction.
Students can prepare results of selected analyses and calculations, present them in groups, and discuss them.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental concepts and axioms of statics
assessment_rules: The portfolio examination totals 100 points, comprising a two-hour written exam (K2) and a written work sample (APS). A maximum of 80 points can be achieved with K2. The APS is offered twice; students are free to participate in both written work samples, with the best-rated work sample counting for a maximum of 20 points.
